la:adj:severus.gloss: severe, serious, strict, stern, stringent, austere, harsh, grave (in demeanor)
senses: severe, serious, strict, stern, stringent, austere, harsh, grave (in demeanor)
la:adj:severus.html:
sĕvērus, a, um, adj.
perh. kindr. with serius
,
serious, grave, strict, austere, stern, severe in aspect, demeanor, conduct, etc. (of persons and things; serius regularly only of things; v. serius; class. and freq.).
Of persons: nam te omnes saevom severumque commemorant,: quam severus!; : civis severus et gravis,; cf.: omnium gravissimus et severissimus, etc.,: Tubero (Stoicus) vitā severus,; cf.: Stoicorum secta severissima,: agricolae,hardended by toil, rugged,: Cures,: Zethus,; cf. in comp.: rumores senum severiorum,.—Of those who live a sober and temperate life: at vos hinc abite, lymphae, Vini pernicies et ad severos Migrate,: adimam cantare severis,; : legis custodes,: neque severus esse (potest) in judicando, qui

alios in se severos esse judices non vult, ; so, judices severi in eos solos,; cf.: severissimos atque integerrimos judices,: ex familiā ad judicandum severissimā,: ubi haec severus te palam laudaveram,: auctor e severissimis,: Aristolaus e severissimis pictoribus fuit, (for which, just before: austerior colore).—

In a bad sense, harsh, rough, crabbed, rigid, severe (rare): Neptunus saevus severusque,: idem acerbe severus in filium, dub. (a passage bracketed by B. and K.): in me severior quam in vos,; : Eumenidum turba, cf. II. B.—
Of things, grave, serious, severe, austere, etc.: severā fronte curas cogitans,: vultus severior et tristior,; cf. : frons,: Falernum, rough, sharp, tart (syn. austerum), : divaeque (Palladis) severas Fronde ligare comas,: animus (opp. mitis),: disciplina maxime severa,: imperia severiora,: judicia severa,: lex,: severiora judicia,: severiores leges,; cf.: Lycurgus severissimarum justissimarumque legum auctor,: imperii severissimi vir,: quod ego dixi per jocum, Id eventurum esse et severum et serium,: linque severa,: paulo severior poena,.—Of style: sententiae graves et severae,: triste et severum genus dicendi,; so ; ; sq.; 10, 1, 131 al.; cf.: severae Musa tragoediae,: fidibus voces crevere severis,.—
Severe, dreadful, gloomy: severus Uncus abest,: silentia noctis,: heims,: amnem Cocyti metuet,; cf. absol.: Si. Accurrite, Ne se interimat ... Me. Hau! voluisti istuc severum facere? this horrible deed, (but in the correct read. is pelage sonora; v. Lachm. ad h. l.).—Hence, adv., in three forms, severe (class.), severiter (anteand post-class.), and severum (post-class.).
sĕvērē, gravely, seriously, austerely, rigidly, severely, : graviter et severe voluptatem secernit a bono,: vetuit (with graviter),: uti judicio,: aestimatae lites,; : vindicare Hiempsalis mortem,: dicere,; ; : domesticam disciplinam regere,.—Comp.: ad aliquem severius scribere,: adhibere aliquem,: coërcere matrimonia,. —Sup.: sunt qui voluptatem severissime contemnant,; so, exacta aetas,: dicere jus,.—
sĕvērĭter, gravely, seriously, severely: sermonem cum aliquo conferre, Titin. ap. ; and in P.; Plaut., acc. to . 1.; .—*
sĕvērum, harshly, austerely: nunc severum vivitur,.

la:noun:severitas.html:
sĕvērĭtas, ātis, f.
1. severus
,
seriousness, gravity, sternness, strictness, severity, in a good and bad sense (class. and very freq.; syn. gravitas): tristis severitas inest in vultu,: severitatem in senectute probo: acerbitatem nullo modo, (opp. lepos); : censorum,; cf. .—Plur.: censorum severitates,: tristitia et in omni re severitas,; cf.: homo ipsā tristitiā et severitate popularis,: si illius comitatem et facilitatem tuae gravitati severitatique asperseris,; so (opp. comitas) ; (opp. mansuetudo et misericordia) ; (opp hilaritas risusque) : T. Torquatus cum illam severitatem in eo filio adhibuit, quem, etc.,: evellere se aculeum severitatis vestrae,: laetissimae vir severitatis,: Catoni severitas dignitatem addiderat,: commodare magnis peccatis severitatem,: summa severitas animadversionis,: exempli,: judiciorum (opp. lenitas ac misericordia),: imperii,; cf.: militarem disciplinam severitatemque minuere, Auct. B. Alex. 48 fin.; 65: nimia emendationis severitas,: disciplinae,: orationis,: hac severitate aurium laetor,this severity of taste,.—
Transf.: etiam corruptissimo in genere magis tamen juvat quaedam ipsius viti severitas,rudeness, crudeness,.

senses: to call off, separate, withdraw or remove
la:verb:sevoco.html:
sē-vŏco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to call apart or aside, to call away to some particular place (class.; a favorite word of Cic.; syn. seduco).
Lit.: sevocare singulos hortarique coepit,: erum,: hunc,: maxime placitam (feminam ad stuprum),: aliquem,: plebem in Aventinum,; cf.: tribuni plebis, ne quis postea populum sevocaret, capite sanxerunt,should call a meeting of the people out of the city,: quid tu te solus e senatu sevocas?separate yourself,.—Less freq. with inanimate objects: haud mediocriter de communi quicquid poterat ad se in privatam domum sevocabat,put aside, withdrew, subtracted,.—
Trop., to call off, separate, withdraw, remove: cura me sevocat a doctis virginibus (i. e. Musis),: animum a negotio omni,: animum a societate et a contagione corporis somno,; cf. : mentem a sensibus,: mentem ab oculis,: ab his non multo secus quam a poëtis haec eloquentia sevocanda est,: quid illuc est, quod ille solus se in consilium sevocat?takes counsel with himself alone,.
